quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When does a motorcycle have less traction for braking?

options.text: When a motorcycle is straight up and down.
When a motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans, such as during a turn, there is less grip available for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: One that helps you avoid road hazards.
One that hides you from other drivers.
One that places you next to another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that helps you avoid road hazards.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid road hazards. Always keep safe space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: Why should you check your mirrors when stopping at an intersection?

options.text: To see if drivers behind you know you are stopping.
To look for dark clouds that show bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see if drivers behind you know you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors to watch for vehicles coming from behind. Make sure drivers see you and respond to your actions.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must let oncoming traffic pass first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop and wait for a signal that lets you turn.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Yes, they have blind spots just like cars.
No, they do not have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they have blind spots just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects steering, which affects your balance.
It prevents you from speeding up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects steering, which affects your balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering difficult, which hurts your balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to work well?

options.text: Block side vision so you focus on the road ahead.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist damage, give clear side views, fasten securely, let air through to stop fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a turn?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before turning. Taking a turn too fast can make you drift out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: They are less dangerous than either one alone.
Their effects can be stronger than either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their effects can be stronger than either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it hard to ride safely. Some drugs become more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do for a quick stop?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time. Look ahead on the road to help you avoid sudden stops.

questions.question: Which color will make you less visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or drab colors.

questions.question: What is a benefit of keeping space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: You can draft off other vehicles better.
You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you time to respond to hazards and room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time?

options.text: Just start riding. Learning by doing is the best way.
Just start riding. Most bikes are the same.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how the bike works.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how the bike works.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding, check the bike's safety and maintenance. Find where everything is. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn its gear pattern.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or a similar tough material for grip and protection.

questions.question: Which of these should NOT be part of a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: A test of the turn signals

questions.explanation: Check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands before riding.

questions.question: If you have been drinking alcohol, you:

options.text: Can ride if you feel you are not impaired

questions.explanation: Do not ride a motorcycle if you have been drinking. It is unsafe even if you are under the legal limit.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping a motorcycle, you should:
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, your ability to safely ride:
questions.explanation: Your riding skills get worse as you drink more alcohol. Do not ride if you have consumed any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a collision, you should:

options.text: Look straight ahead at your motorcycle
Be unwilling to move to avoid hazards
Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your motorcycle
questions.explanation: Look ahead at least 10 to 15 seconds on your path of travel. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: A good lane position should:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen
Place you in other drivers' blind spots
Invite other drivers to share your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your ability to see and be seen
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and be seen. Avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and surface hazards. Keep other drivers from sharing your lane and maintain an escape route.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may increase danger by encouraging them to tailgate at the higher speed.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. Nothing else speeds up this process.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your riding ability?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride safely. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic ahead will merge.

questions.question: What is the best clothing for a motorcyclist?

options.text: Clothing that protects you in a crash.
Clothing that does not stand out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing that protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you in a crash, keep you comfortable, and help other drivers see you.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: Why is it hard to ride right when it starts raining?

options.text: Other drivers may not react fast enough.

questions.explanation: When it first rains, oil from vehicles mixes with water on the road, making it very slippery.

questions.question: What helps prevent serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection in a crash. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face from injury.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead is slippery when wet.
